metadata.title: The Relationship Between Students’ Awareness of Environmental Issues and Attitudes Toward Science and Epistemological Beliefs—Moderating Effect of Informal Science Activities

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2015 student questionnaire indices for a subset of BSJG (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Guangdong) students (n=9841 unweighted cases; weighted N reported as 1,331,794). The authors state that weighted likelihood estimation (WLE) was performed on students’ answers based on IRT and that resulting indices were standardized using the mean and standard deviation of OECD countries, which is consistent with PISA’s scaling approach rather than explicit reporting of a student sampling weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT). For the regression/correlation analyses reported in Tables 1–2, the manuscript does not specify whether complex survey sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in SPSS 25. Because the paper does not report a weight variable name or replicate design method, weighting beyond PISA’s WLE/scaling cannot be confirmed from the text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2015 BSJG (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Guangdong) student data; analytic sample comprised 15-year-old students selected via two-stage stratified sampling. The authors report an overall missing rate of 0.4%–7.1% and applied multiple imputation after 5 imputations/interpolations in SPSS to obtain 9841 cases for analysis.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2015 Science (15-year-olds), BSJG subset (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Guangdong), China
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple regression: R²=0.332; Environmental awareness β=0.059 (p<0.05); Interaction β=0.016 (p<0.05); Interest in science β=0.296 (p<0.05); Epistemological beliefs β=0.225 (p<0.05); Science self-efficacy β=0.060 (p<0.05); ESCS β=0.041 (p<0.05). Correlation: ENVAWARE–JOYSCIE r=0.340 (p<0.01).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2015 Science data for the BSJG subset of China, the study leveraged environmental awareness, informal science activities, and their interaction (plus related attitudes and ESCS) to analyze enjoyment of science, finding that environmental awareness had a significant positive association and that informal science activities significantly moderated this relationship (interaction β=0.016, p<0.05). This indicates that strengthening students’ environmental issue awareness and providing opportunities for informal science participation may increase enjoyment of science, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2015 Science (15-year-olds), BSJG subset (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Guangdong), China
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple regression: R²=0.303; Environmental awareness β=0.142 (p<0.05); Interaction β=0.006 (not significant after Bonferroni correction); Enjoyment of science β=0.258 (p<0.05); Science self-efficacy β=0.042 (p<0.05); Epistemological beliefs β=0.082 (p<0.05); ESCS β=-0.036 (p<0.05). Correlation: ENVAWARE–INTBRSCI r=0.373 (p<0.01).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2015 Science data for the BSJG subset of China, the study leveraged environmental awareness, informal science activities, and their interaction (plus enjoyment, self-efficacy, epistemological beliefs, and ESCS) to analyze interest in science, finding that environmental awareness was positively associated with interest (β=0.142, p<0.05) but the interaction with informal science activities was not significant after Bonferroni correction (β=0.006). This indicates that environmental awareness may support students’ science interest directly, while informal science activities may not further strengthen that specific link, suggesting targeted attention to SSI awareness-building.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2015 Science (15-year-olds), BSJG subset (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Guangdong), China
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple regression: R²=0.284; Environmental awareness β=0.264 (p<0.05); Interaction β=0.016 (p<0.05); Enjoyment of science β=0.108 (p<0.05); Interest in science β=0.087 (p<0.05); Epistemological beliefs β=0.104 (p<0.05); ESCS β=0.105 (p<0.05). Correlation: ENVAWARE–SCIEEFF r=0.401 (p<0.01).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2015 Science data for the BSJG subset of China, the study leveraged environmental awareness, informal science activities, and their interaction (plus enjoyment, interest, epistemological beliefs, and ESCS) to analyze science self-efficacy, finding that environmental awareness had a strong positive association (β=0.264, p<0.05) and that informal science activities significantly moderated this relationship (interaction β=0.016, p<0.05). This indicates that pairing SSI-related environmental awareness with opportunities for informal science engagement may help students feel more capable in science tasks, though the moderation effect size is small and causality cannot be inferred.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2015 Science (15-year-olds), BSJG subset (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Guangdong), China
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple regression: R²=0.194; Environmental awareness β=0.098 (p<0.05); Interaction β=0.004 (not significant); Enjoyment of science β=0.247 (p<0.05); Interest in science β=0.104 (p<0.05); Science self-efficacy β=0.064 (p<0.05); ESCS β=0.087 (p<0.05). Correlation: ENVAWARE–EPIST r=0.290 (p<0.01).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2015 Science data for the BSJG subset of China, the study leveraged environmental awareness, informal science activities, and their interaction (plus enjoyment, interest, self-efficacy, and ESCS) to analyze science epistemological beliefs, finding that environmental awareness was positively associated with epistemological beliefs (β=0.098, p<0.05) but the interaction with informal science activities was not significant (β=0.004). This indicates that SSI-linked environmental awareness may be a more direct lever for strengthening epistemological beliefs, while informal science activities may not meaningfully change how awareness translates into epistemological sophistication.

data.outcome_summary: This study used PISA 2015 science data for 15-year-old students from the BSJG subset of China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Guangdong; N=9841; weighted N reported as 1,331,794). Students’ environmental awareness, informal science activities, and ESCS were related to four science attitude/epistemology outcomes using correlation and multiple regression models in SPSS 25, with multiple imputation for missing values (5 imputations). Environmental awareness showed significant positive correlations with enjoyment (r=0.340), interest (r=0.373), self-efficacy (r=0.401), and epistemological beliefs (r=0.290). In regression, environmental awareness predicted all four outcomes (R²: 0.332 enjoyment; 0.303 interest; 0.284 self-efficacy; 0.194 epistemological beliefs), while informal science activities significantly moderated only the enjoyment and self-efficacy relationships (interaction β=0.016, p<0.05) and not interest or epistemological beliefs (interaction not significant after Bonferroni). Limitations include cross-sectional design and self-reported measures, so findings indicate associations and moderation rather than causal effects.
